findings.issue: The docstring and the guide say the TMPDIR 'is left in place afterwards, and removing it is the task's teardown, which finds it through that record'. No teardown exists: nothing under plugins/audit/scripts removes the scratch or reads a *.tmpdir file (the same paragraph admits 'nothing in the drive reads the path back today'). The TMPDIRs, which hold whatever fixtures a writer's suites built, previously sat in the project's gitignored state dir and now accumulate in the machine's system temp, once per session (writer and reviewer, every round), with a record file nobody consumes. The sentence names a mechanism that is not there.
findings.resolution: Reword to say no teardown reads the record yet, and file a follow-up task for the drive to remove the TMPDIRs the scratch records name when it closes the task (or have the runner remove its own TMPDIR after the child exits, since the stream already carries the evidence).

findings.issue: A parent temp directory with a .git above it is refused with exit 5 and no other root is tried. That blocks a user who worked before this change: TMPDIR set inside the project, or a Windows user whose TEMP (under the profile) has a dotfiles repo at the profile root. The task says to 'refuse to start when no temp root outside a checkout exists'; the diff refuses when the one gettempdir() returned is inside a checkout, even though /tmp or /var/tmp may exist outside one. The refusal does name the directory and the remedy, and ras34 pins that it makes nothing, so this is a deliberate narrowing, not a silent one.
findings.resolution: Either keep the strict reading and say in the guide that a caller whose temp is inside a checkout must repoint TMPDIR, or try the remaining tempfile candidates (/tmp, /var/tmp) and refuse only when none is outside a checkout.

findings.issue: The suite's root comes from tempfile.mkdtemp under the ambient TMPDIR, and every _run now makes its parent temp under that root. If the suite is run with TMPDIR inside a checkout (the P137.3 scenario) the new refusal fires in every case, so the whole file goes red with exit 5 instead of naming the cause, and ras32's '_git_above(seen_tmp) is None' premise is no longer independent of the environment.
findings.resolution: Assert up front that root has no .git ancestor (one case naming the ambient TMPDIR), so a bad environment reads as that and not as 40 unrelated failures.
